title: Circadian entrainment, sleep need and shift tolerance for the person day-rhythm model, including a 24 h 39 m Mars sol
question: What do the peer-reviewed chronobiology and sleep-medicine literatures establish about sleep–wake regulation (the two-process model), the population distribution of chronotypes and sleep need, tolerance of night/rotating shift work, and — critically — human entrainment to a Mars sol of 24 h 39 m 35 s, so that NOXIA's deterministic day-rhythm model is calibrated to real physiology? Concretely: is an 8-hour contiguous sleep window with bedtimes spread only 21:00–01:00 and a sleep-need range of 6–9 hours consistent with measured distributions; does a fixed 12-hour flip approximate real night-shift adaptation; and what does the evidence say about whether a settlement can share one colony clock ('tick mod 24') versus needing per-location local time and an explicit Mars-sol adaptation rather than ignoring it?
why_now: NOXIA-LIVING-0007 (accepted 2026-10-08, code in lib/game/population/circadian.ts and merged circadian tests) explicitly records two unresolved items: 'Ein Mars-Sol von 24,66 Stunden ist nicht abgebildet' and, under Offen, 'Ortszeit je Siedlung und Mars-Sol'. Mars is a core NOXIA setting, and the model currently hard-codes DAY_TICKS = 24 with a single shared colony time, so the gap is an acknowledged TODO that directly shapes simulation and narrative plausibility.
real_world_anchor: Human chronobiology and sleep medicine: the two-process model of sleep regulation, chronotype and sleep-need distributions in healthy adults, shift-work sleep disorder and adaptation rates, and Mars-sol (24 h 39 m 35 s) circadian entrainment/adaptation studies from analog and mission-research settings.
novelty_reason: Not covered by any prior topic. RES-20260828-CF5AF859 concerns partial-gravity effects on reproduction, prenatal/neonatal development and gravity transitions, not circadian rhythm, sleep architecture or sol-length entrainment. No previous research question addresses shift work, chronotype spread or Mars-sol entrainment.
